ClassDefinitionAligned withStored as
PersonThe wardrobe's owner, who logs what they wear. In this data set there is exactly one.schema:Person
GarmentOne physical piece of clothing, footwear or accessory owned at some point since tracking began. Two identical items bought together are separate garments (e.g. "Diesel gray 01" and "Diesel gray 02").schema:ProductGarments
CategoryA kind of clothing that groups garments, from a fixed list in a standard order.schema:DefinedTermgarments.category
Ownership period derivedThe days a garment counts as owned: from its purchase date (at the earliest the start of tracking) to its divest date, inclusive; open-ended while it is still active.
Wear dayOne calendar day of the log and the set of garments worn on it.Wear log
Wear derivedOne garment worn on one day. Wearing a garment twice on the same day is one wear.prov:Activity
TagA descriptive label from a fixed vocabulary, e.g. second hand or Hanko. Tags never change a calculation.schema:DefinedTermgarments.tags
Material composition derivedThe fibres a garment's main part is made of, with their shares (summing to 100 %), read from its free-text materials label.
FibreA textile or material, e.g. cotton, wool, polyester, leather.
Fibre classOne of four groups of fibres: natural, regenerated cellulose, synthetic or other.
Comparison itemAn item of other everyday spending (transport, subscriptions, tools…) with a monthly cost and a frequency of use, shown next to the clothing categories for comparison.Comparison items

Metrics (semantic model)

Every figure the app and the MCP server compute: its definition, formula, grain, unit, how the chosen date range applies, the decisions behind it, and the code and tests that implement it. Shared rules: wears outside a garment's ownership period never count; dates are inclusive; one month is 30.5 days.

Times worn times-worn

Wears of the garment within the range (and within its ownership period), plus pre-tracking wears when the range starts on the start of tracking.

Cost per wear (category) category-cost-per-wear

The sum of the prices of the category's garments owned at any point in the range, divided by the sum of their lifetime wears. Unworn garments count with their full price and no wears; if none of them has ever been worn, the sum of prices is divided by 1 (as an unworn garment costs its full price). Garments without a price are left out. No Total row value.

Σ price / max(1, Σ lifetime-wears), over the category's garments owned during the range with a price

Daily cost daily-cost

For each logged day in the range with wears: the sum of the lifetime cost per wear of the garments worn and owned that day (unknown prices count 0); "final" when all of them are divested. Average - the mean of 30 consecutive logged days centred on the day (days i−14 … i+15), so days without wears are skipped.

Σ garment-cost-per-wear over garments worn on d; average(i) = mean(cost[i−14 .. i+15])

Decisions

D-1: Public pages get the full day-by-day log 2026-10-09

Public pages and the MCP server read one world-readable document with all garments and the full wear log, and compute every metric from it, rather than precomputed summaries.

Why: Any metric for any date range can be computed in the browser with one document read.

Affects: Public wardrobe data

D-2: Cost per wear is always lifetime 2026-10-09

A garment's cost per wear is price / all its wears over its whole ownership, regardless of the chosen date range, even when wears after the range lower it. A category's cost per wear for a range is Σ price / Σ lifetime wears over its garments owned at any point in the range, unworn garments included (divided by 1 if none has ever been worn).

Why: The concept must be treated consistently - a garment has one cost per wear, and unused purchases must not disappear from a category's cost.

Amended: 2026-10-16 (Olof): the category figure was the average of the garments' cost per wear weighted by wears in the range, over garments worn in the range, which left unworn garments out entirely. Now pooled over lifetime wears with unworn garments included. Raises categories with unused garments (e.g. Socks +43 % in 2025) and changes Yearly cost, Turnover and the monthly cost comparison with it.

Affects: Cost per wear (garment), Cost per wear (category), Daily cost

D-3: Small multiples for per-category charts 2026-10-09

Charts that show several categories use one small chart per category on a shared scale.

Why: The original 12-colour palette fails colour-blind and contrast checks.

D-4: Garment details are edited in the app 2026-10-09

Garment details are edited in the app and stored in Firestore, which is their source of truth.

Affects: Garments

Q-1: Daily cost definition 2026-10-09

Daily cost = Σ over garments worn that day (and owned then) of their lifetime cost per wear; "final" when every one of them is divested; plus a rolling mean centred on the day.

Affects: Daily cost

R-15: Cut-over to logging in the app 2026-10-09

The app is the source of truth for wears from 2026-10-10; the Sheet holds the log through 2026-10-09 and is retired.

Affects: Wear log, Google Sheet (retired)

R-28: Nightly backups 2026-10-10

A nightly job exports all owner data to a private repository with a read-only account.

Affects: Nightly backups

2026-10-08-ranges: Metrics work for any date range 2026-10-08

All metric functions take a date range; the per-day data stays available rather than being pre-aggregated.

Affects: Date range
